text.p: - The government said it would raise electricity prices by 4.9 percent from February.
- The parliament on Thursday elected most parliamentary bodies.

- Ljubljana's mayor Dimitrij Rupel called for the resignation of Janez Sodrznik, director of the City Management Board, after the Accountancy Court, the central body controlling public finances, found irregularities in the city's accounts.
- Prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek on Thursday continued coalition talks and is expected to introduce proposals for a coalition agreement on Friday.
- About a quarter of Slovenia's GDP consists of labour that is not registered by tax autorities, experts said.
- Dutch firm Cosun bougth 25 percent of shares of Slovenia's sugar producer Tovarna Sladkorja Ormoz.
- Trading company Mercator said its 1995 pre-tax profit rose to 670 million tolars ($4,6 million) from 416 million in 1995.
- Most companies listed on the Ljubljana Stock Exchange said they were satisfied with expected results for 1996.
- The Office for Protection of Competition said it would probably approve a proposed agreement between all Slovenian banks that will reduce deposit interest rates from April.
